column2: with good fuel-sticks he would offer and gain incomparable poetic power. Now I shall tell of Savitri, Brahma's beloved, O best of Brahmins,
by worshipping whom Brahma created the worlds, moving and unmoving: Lakshmi, Maya, Kama first, "Savitri" in the dative,
ending in "svaha" is declared the mantra of Savitri, eight-syllabled. Its sage is Brahma; the metre Gayatri; the deity is declared:
Savitri of all the gods, called Savitri. With words ending in the heart, Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Ishvara, Sadashiva,
and with "sarvatmane" in the dative, the conception of the limbs is held. She is bright as heated gold, blazing with Brahma's radiance,
her body like a thousand midday summer suns, with a gentle smile and gracious face, adorned with jewelled ornaments,
wearing a fire-purified garment, eager to favour devotees, giver of happiness, liberation and all prosperity, auspicious,
whose form is the seed of the Veda — he should meditate on the chaste mother of the Vedas. Having meditated thus, the wise one in a diagram with a bright triangular pericarp,
on the solar seat, should worship the Goddess with the nine powers beginning with Dipta. Conceiving the form with the root, he should worship the Goddess in it;
in three corners Brahmi and the other powers are to be worshipped; outside, Aditya and the rest with Usha in order are to be worshipped.
Then having worshipped the six limbs and on the filaments by rule: Prahladini, Prabha, Nitya, Vishvambhara,
Vilasini, Prabhavati, Jaya, Shanta he should worship; Kanti, Durga, Sarasvati, then Vidyarupa,
Vishala, Isha, Vyapini, Vimala he should worship; Tamopaharini, Sukshma, Vishvayoni, Jayavaha,
Padmalaya, Para, Shobha, Brahmarupa he should then worship; the Brahmi and others as protectors outside, with the marks stated.
Then he should worship the planets outside, with Shakra and the others with their weapons. Thus he should worship the Goddess with ten enclosures.
He should chant eight hundred thousand and offer a thousand with sesame; freed from all sins he obtains long life.
Offering ten thousand red lotuses soaked in three sweet things, Mahalakshmi will be his within six months, without doubt.
He should offer with flowers of the Brahma-tree for outer radiance. What need to say more? Properly accomplished, she is chaste;
this knowledge becomes for practitioners a wish-granting cow, O sage. Now I shall tell you a supreme, wonderful secret:
the "Savitri-panjara" (cage of Savitri), the protection of men in every way. She is attached to sky-hair and curls, adorned with a fair crown,
her brows curved like clouds, her faces Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva; her ears reaching to Jupiter and Venus, with eyes of moon, sun and fire,
with nostrils joined with ida, pingala and the fine breaths; her lips the two twilights, her tongue shining with speech;
her neck the twilights and the sun-jewel, her arms the winds; her heart attached to the rain-god, her circle named Vasu,
wandering in the belly of space, with the inner path at the navel; her thighs called Prajapati, her waist in Indrani,
her thighs shining with the Malaya and Meru mountains, the best of rivers; her knees... called Vaishvadeva;
her feet, toenails and hairs marked with earth, serpents and trees; her limbs the forms of planets, signs, stars and yogas,
by tithis, months, seasons and fortnights, made of signals and winks, covered with a veil called twilight, variegated by maya,
bright like blazing fire of time, shining like lightning, like ten million suns, cool as ten million moons,
seated in the middle of the orb of nectar, made of dense bliss and nectar, beyond speech, beyond mind's reach, giver of boons, mother of the Vedas,
made of the moving and unmoving, eternal, endowed with the imperishable Brahman: having meditated, one with the Self non-different should place the Savitri-panjara.
The sage of the five-fold (panjara) is "So 'ham", the metre called Vikriti; the deity is the Supreme Hamsa, the Supreme Brahman and others;
the application is declared for dharma, wealth, desire and liberation. He should perform limb-placing with the six-limb deity mantras.
The wise one should make it all-pervading with the three-fold root; he should meditate on the deity told before, with form and qualities.
Three-footed, born of Hari, facing east, called the Brahma-weapon, rich in twenty-four principles — may she protect the eastern direction for me.
Four-footed, the Brahma-staff, Brahmani, facing south, joined with twenty-six principles — may she protect my southern direction.
Facing west, five-footed, of fifty principles' form, marked with the Brahma-head — may she always protect the west for me.
Gentle-faced, rich in the fourth of Brahma, of Atharva-Angiras nature, six-footed, made of sixty principles and digits, may she protect the north.
Formed of fifty letters, nine-footed, hundred-syllabled, space, abiding in Vedanta — may she protect my upward head.
Lightning-like, the Brahma-twilight, riding a deer, four-armed, bearing bow, arrows, shield and sword — may she protect my south-east.
Brahmi, Kumari, Gayatri, red-bodied, riding a swan, bearing a water-pot, rosary, and ladle and spoon — may she protect the south-west.
White-coloured Savitri, young, riding a bull, bearing skull, trident and rosary — may she protect the north-west.
Dark Sarasvati, aged, Vaishnavi seated on Garuda, with conch, discus and protection in her hands — may she protect my north-east.
Four-armed, mother of the gods, fair-bodied, riding a lion, with boon, protection, sword and shield in her arms — may she protect the lower direction.
Standing at their sides, each with her own vehicle, weapons and ornaments, standing in their own directions, may they protect, with the planets, powers and limbs.
The deities of mantras, the deities presiding over the mudras — may they, as pervaders, protect me from the soles of my feet to the crown of my head.
This Savitri-panjara has been told to you truly by me. At the twilights daily with devotion, especially at the time of chanting,
it is to be recited with effort by one wishing enjoyment and liberation. Bhutida, Bhuvana, Vani, Mahavasumati, Mahi,
Hiranyajanani, Nanda, Savisarga, Tapasvini, Yashasvini, Sati, Satya, Vedavit, Chinmayi, Shubha,
Vishva, Turya, Vareniya, Nisrini, Yamuna, Bhuva, Moda, Devi, Varishtha, Dhi, Shanti, Mati, Mahi,
Dhishana, Yogini, Yukta, Nadi, Prajnapracodani, Daya, Yamini, Padma, Rohini, Ramani, Jaya,
Senamukhi, Samamayi, Bagala, Doshavarjita, Maya, Prajna, Para, Dogdhri, Manini, Poshini, Kriya,
Jyotsna, Tirthamayi, Ramya, Saumya, Amritamayi, Brahmi, Haimi, Bhujangi, Vashini, Sundari, Vani,
Omkarahasini, Sarva, Sudha, Shadgunavati, Maya, Svadha, Rama, Tanvi, Ripughni, Rakshani, Sati,
Haimi, Tara, Vidhugati, Vishaghni, Varanana, Amara, Tirthada, Diksha, Durdharsha, Rogaharini,
Nanapapa-nrishamsaghni, Shatpadi, Vajrini, Rani, Yogini, Vamala, Satya, Abala, Balada, Jaya,
Gomati, Jahnavi, Rajavi, Tapani, Jatavedasa, Achira, Vrishtida — to be known; Ritatantra, Ritatmika,
Sarvakamadugha, Saumya, free of ego, two-footed, four-footed, three-footed and six-footed,
eight-footed, nine-footed, thousand-eyed, of the nature of the imperishable syllable — the man who recites these hundred and eight names of Savitri
becomes long-lived, happy, with sons, victorious and modest. This has been told to you, O Brahmin: the marks of the five Prakritis,
preceded by worship of the mantras, fulfilling all desires of the world.
Outside the lotus the attendant powers are to be worshipped: first the two Anangas, then Anangamadana,
Madanatura, Bhavanavega, then Bhuvanapalika, Sarvashishira, Anangavedana, Anangamekhala,
holding in their lotus hands a cup, a palm-leaf fan, betel, a shining umbrella, two chowries, cloth and flowers —
he should worship outside the lords of the world blazing with all ornaments, and outside them Vajra and the rest; thus he should worship the Goddess.
The mantra-knower, having offered with the three sweet things and best ashvattha fuel-sticks, would soon subdue Brahmins; by a lotus-offering, kings;
with palasha flowers, the wives of the wise; and with water chanted twenty-five times, a bath each day.
Whoever sprinkles himself becomes endowed with all good fortune. A man who drinks water chanted twenty-five times in the morning
gains great wisdom and becomes first among poets. Taking saffron mixed with camphor and aloe, well prepared,
he should make a tilaka: unsurpassed for subduing a king. Making a doll of rice-flour with sweet things,
chanted over and infused with life, he should eat it on Sunday: he subdues a king, a woman or a man.
Standing in water up to the neck, looking at the sun rising from the water, chanting the mantra three thousand times, he gets the desired bride.
The mantra-knower should eat food so consecrated, for fame of prosperity. Maya written with ash with the object on a board and the like,
showing the yantra at that time, a pregnant woman bears easily. This is declared the Bhuvaneshi, born from a thousand arms,
giver of enjoyment and liberation to men who remember her, O best of Brahmins. Then in another kalpa, O Brahmin, once there was the buffalo-demon,
who conquered the guardians of the world and enjoyed the three worlds. Then the afflicted gods took refuge in Vaikuntha.
Then the goddess Mahalakshmi, from the energy arisen from the bodies of the discus-bearer and others, became Shri in a body, O best of sages, pervading the three worlds.
Having herself slain the buffalo-demon and the rest, the Lady of the world reached the lotus forest, giver of desires to her worshippers.
I shall tell her worship in brief; hear, O Brahmin: the head adorned with a bindu, with "mrityu" and "krodha" and the teacher...
the seed mantra of Shri is declared, giving desires to worshippers. Its sage is Bhrigu, the metre Nivrit, the deity Shri.
With the seed rich in six long vowels he should make the six limbs in order. Then he should meditate on Shri, the giver of prosperity, to be known by the world,
golden-bright, being sprinkled by four white elephants held up in their own trunks with golden jars of nectar, seated on a lotus,
her hands holding boon, protection, lotus and garland, clad in silk, crowned. He should chant a hundred thousand and offer a thousand.
Having worshipped with fragrant flowers and with lotuses soaked in honey, he should conceive the form with the root on the seat told for Mahalakshmi.
He should worship the limbs as before and then in the directions on the petals: Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha,
snow-white, yellow, tamala-dark, and Indra-blue, clad in yellow, four-armed, bearing conch, discus, mace and lotus.
At the corners on the petals he should worship the elephants Damaka and others: Damaka, Pundarika, Guggula, Kuranthaka.
On the right of the Goddess he should worship the conch treasure with his wife, bright as pearl and ruby, with slightly smiling lotus faces,
embracing each other, bearing conch and lotus, marked on the head by conches from which jewel rain flows;
Tundila, the conch treasure, Vasudhara with firm breasts; on the left he should worship the lotus treasure with his beloved,
vermilion-bright, clasped in arms, with red lotus and lily, marked on the head by lotuses from which jewel rain falls;
Tundila, the lotus treasure, Tattva and Vasumati. On the petal-tips he should worship all around these, beginning with Balaka:
Balaki, Vimala, Kamala, Vanamalika, Vibhishika, Malika, Shankari, Vasumalika,
each holding a pair of lotuses, bright as pearl necklaces. At the end he should worship the lords of the worlds, and outside them the weapons Vajra and the rest.
The best of practitioners who thus worships the Goddess by rule becomes rich in wealth and grain and gains blameless prosperity.
Standing in water up to the chest, he should chant this mantra, meditating on the one in the sun: three hundred thousand — he becomes a dwelling of Lakshmi.
The practitioner who chants three hundred thousand at the foot of a bilva tree in Vishnu's house obtains the heap of wealth he wishes.
By offering rice soaked in ghee in an ashoka fire he would subdue the world; with rice soaked in honey in a khadira fire,
a king is soon subdued and Mahalakshmi increases. Living in the shade of a bilva tree, eating food mixed with bilva-ghee,
having offered for three years with its fruits or with lotuses, the best of practitioners surely sees Mahalakshmi with his eyes.
Then in another kalpa two demons, Shumbha and Nishumbha, plunderers of the gods' kingdom, were born, thorns of the world.
Then praised by Shakra and the others who had lost their offices, O sage, the goddess Mahasarasvati descended.
On the very holy Himalaya, in a lovely mountain region, having slain Shumbha and the others and worshipped by the gods,
giving a boon, the Goddess entered the lake named Manasa. I shall tell her mantra; hear attentively, O sage:
Jnanamrita, with a moon, adorned with a forehead crossed by bindu: the Vagbija; with it the best practitioner should make the limbs.
Its sage is Sadashiva, the metre Anushtubh is declared; the deity is called Vak (Speech), giver of desires to worshippers.
He should constantly meditate on the Goddess in white garments, white, holding lute and book, endowed with divine ornaments.
On the Mahasarasvati seat he should conceive the form with the root; he should worship the Goddess in it with the enclosures beginning with the limbs.
First the enclosure of the limbs; afterward Ambika and the others are told; the second is told with the Mothers; the third and others with the eight powers;
the fourth and fifth are told with thirty-two powers; the sixth is remembered with sixty-four powers and the lords of the worlds;
the seventh again of these with their weapons is the eighth enclosure. Thus the world-mother, glorious, called Vagbhava, is to be worshipped.
In the places stated before the practitioner should worship the limbs: Ambika, Vagbhava, Durga, Shri-shakti with the marks stated;
then Brahma and the others are to be worshipped: Karali, Vikarali, Uma, Sarasvati, Shri, Durga, Lakshmi, Dhriti, Smriti,
Shraddha, Medha, Rati, Kanti, Arya — sixteen powers. Dark, holding sword and shield, well adorned, they are to be worshipped:
Vishaghni, Pushti, Prajna, Sinivali, Kuhu, Rudravirya, Prabha, Nanda, Poshana, Vriddhida, Shubha,
Kalaratri, Maharatri, Bhadrakali, Kapardini, Vikriti, Dandini, Mundini, Indukhanda, Shikhandini,
Nishumbhamathani, Chandamundavinashini, Indrani, Rudrani, the half-bodied of Shankara,
Nari, Narayani, Trishulini, Palini, Ambika and Hradini: thirty-two white powers,
with discus in hand, with demonic faces, to be worshipped, adorned with lovely ornaments: Pingalaksi, Vishalakshi, Samriddhi, Buddhi,
Shraddha, Svaha, Svadha, Bhiksha, Maya, Sanjna, Vasundhara, Trilokadhatri, Gayatri, Savitri, Tridasheshvari,
Sarupa, Bahurupa, Skandamata, Shrutipriya, Vimala, Kamala, then Aruni, again Aruni,
Prakriti, Vikriti, Srishti, Sthiti, Samhriti, Sandhya, Mata, Sati, Hamsi, Mardika, Vajrika, Para,
Devamata, Bhagavati, Devaki, Kamalasana, Trimukhi, Saptavadana, Surasuravimardini,
Lamboshthi, Urdhvakeshi, Bahushishna, Vrikodari, Ratharekha, then Shashirekha, and another,
Gaganavega, Pavanavega, Vega, then Bhuvanapala, then Madanatura,
Ananga, Anangavadana, Anangamekhala, Anangakusuma, Vishvarupa, Surabhayankari,
Akshobhya, Saptavahini, Vajrarupa, Shuchivrata, and Varada, then Vagishi: sixty-four are declared,
all bearing bows and arrows, flame-tongued, of great radiance, tusked, with upward hair, their minds set on battle.
There is nothing equal to Ekadashi in destroying sin. Even if observed by pretext, O king, it does not show the sun's son (Yama).
This gives heaven and liberation, kingdom and sons, a good wife, health of the body.
Not the Ganga, not Gaya, O king, not Kashi, not Pushkara, nor the Kairava field, nor Reva, nor Devika,
nor Yamuna and Chandrabhaga are holy in comparison to Hari's day, O king. Without effort, O king, Hari's abode is attained.
Having kept the vigil at night and fasted on Hari's day, a man freed from all sins goes to Vishnu's world.
Ten of the mother's side, ten, O king, of the father's, ten of the wife's side, he would uplift, as well as men;
and himself too, O king, he would take to Vishnu's city. This is like a wish-jewel or a treasure,
like a wish-tree or like Vedic words. Those men who, O best of men, take refuge in Dvadashi
are born with two-armed forms and with serpent-enemy (Garuda) as vehicle, garlanded, in yellow clothes, they go to Hari's abode.
Such is the power of Dvadashi told by me, O king: fire to the terrible fuel of sin.
Hari's day is always to be fasted by men devoted to dharma, wishing for abundant enjoyments, sons, grandsons and the like.

The mortal who here honours Hari's day with respect, O best of men, does not enter a mother's womb again; though full of many sins, wittingly or unwittingly he goes to the endless abode of Vishnu, the Lord of the world.
The measure of tithi, O best of Brahmins, is by the moon and the sun; the experts in time know time by knowledge of the courses of moon and sun.
By the fault of contact with the earlier one, those (tithis) are not fit for worship; the knowers avoid them, O twice-born, for four watches.
Now I shall tell the order of the rule of bathing and worship. By day one does not obtain purity; then it is done at night.
All the day's duties are to be done at the start of night. This rule is told by me for those who fast.
O best of Brahmins, on the short Dvadashi at the dawn, bathing and worship with gifts and offerings should be done.
In the breaking of the fast on the thirteenth, a man surely obtains the fruit of the earth, or even more than a hundred sacrifices.
For this reason, O Brahmins, one should bathe at dawn with offerings to the ancestors, without having seen the Dvadashi day.
This Dvadashi, when transgressed by men, causes great loss; it takes away dharma like an unbathed Sarasvati.
Whether in decrease or increase, or at sunrise, the Dvadashi is to be fasted, being holy; the one joined with the earlier one is to be avoided.
The Brahmin said: "O Suta, when Dvadashi arises joined with the earlier one, how should men keep the fast, tell me?"
When the fast day is spoiled by the earlier one, and on the second day there is not even a little of the Ekadashi tithi...
